source_text:
Σὺ γὰρ τὴν ἀέναον τοῦ κόσμου σύστασιν διὰ τῶν ἐνεργουμένων ἐφανεροποίησας: σύ, κύριε, τὴν οἰκουμένην ἔκτισας, ὁ πιστὸς ἐν πάσαις ταῖς γενεαῖς, δίκαιος ἐν τοῖς κρίμασιν, θαυμαστὸς ἐν ἰσχύϊ καὶ μεγαλοπρεπείᾳ, ὁ σοφὸς ἐν τῷ κτίζειν καὶ συνετὸς ἐν τῷ τὰ γενόμενα ἑδράσαι, ὁ ἀγαθὸς ἐν τοῖς ὁρωμένοις καὶ χρηστὸς ἐν τοῖς πεποιθόσιν ἐπὶ σέ, ἐλεῆμον καὶ οἰκτίρμον, ἄφες ἡμῖν τὰς ἀνομίας ἡμῶν καὶ τὰς ἀδικίας καὶ τὰ παραπτώματα καὶ πλημμελείας.
μὴ λογίσῃ πᾶσαν ἁμαρτίαν δούλων σου καὶ παιδισκῶν, ἀλλὰ καθάρισον ἡμᾶς τὸν καθαρισμὸν τῆς σῆς ἀληθείας, καὶ κατεύθυνον τὰ διαβήματα ἡμῶν ἐν ὁσιότητι καρδίας πορεύεσθαι καὶ ποιεῖν τὰ καλὰ καὶ εὐάρεστα ἐνώπιόν σου καὶ ἐνώπιον τῶν ἀρχόντων ἡμῶν.
ναί, δέσποτα, ἐπίφανον τὸ πρόσωπόν σου ἐφ̓ ἡμᾶς εἰς ἀγαθὰ ἐν εἰρήνῃ, εἰς τὸ σκεπασθῆναι ἡμᾶς τῇ χειρί σου τῇ κραταιᾷ καὶ ῥυσθῆναι ἀπὸ πάσης ἁμαρτίας τῷ βραχίονί σου τῷ ὑψηλῷ, καὶ ῥῦσαι ἡμᾶς ἀπὸ τῶν μισούντων ἡμᾶς ἀδίκως.
δὸς ὁμόνοιαν καὶ εἰρήνην ἡμῖν τε καὶ πᾶσιν τοῖς κατοικοῦσιν τὴν γῆν, καθὼς ἔδωκας τοῖς πατράσιν ἡμῶν, ἐπικαλουμένων σε αὐτῶν ὁσίως ἐν πίστει καὶ ἀληθείᾳ, ὑπηκόους γινομένους τῷ παντοκράτορι καὶ ἐνδόξῳ ὀνόματί σου, τοῖς τε ἄρχουσιν καὶ ἡγουμένοις ἡμῶν ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς.
thought_title: Prayer for cleansing, guidance, and peace
orientation: The Roman church is praying to God, continuing a long prayer of petition that began earlier in the letter, asking for forgiveness, cleansing, guidance, and peace for themselves and all people.
pass_a_gloss: For you the everlasting constitution of the world through the things being worked you made manifest; you, Lord, the inhabited world you created, the faithful [one] in all the generations, just in the judgments, wonderful in strength and magnificence, the wise [one] in the creating and intelligent in the having established the things that have come to be, the good [one] in the things seen and kind to the [ones] having trusted in you, merciful and compassionate, forgive us our lawless deeds and our injustices and the transgressions and offenses. Do not count every sin of your male slaves and female slaves, but cleanse us [with] the cleansing of your truth, and make straight our steps in holiness of heart to walk and to do the good and pleasing [things] before you and before our rulers. Yes, Master, make your face shine upon us for good [things] in peace, for the being sheltered us by your hand the mighty [one] and being rescued from every sin by your arm the high [one], and rescue us from the [ones] hating us unjustly. Give harmony and peace to us and to all the [ones] dwelling on the earth, just as you gave to our fathers, [when] they called upon you holily in faith and truth, [for us] to become obedient to the almighty and glorious name of you, and to the rulers and leaders of us on the earth.

choices.english: the everlasting constitution of the world
choices.why: Keeps the noun 'constitution' for σύστασις to preserve the sense of ordered structure, and 'everlasting' for ἀέναον rather than 'eternal' to reflect the flowing, perpetual nuance.
rejected: the eternal order of the world
the perpetual structure of the cosmos

choices.why: Preserves the passive/middle participle force of things being effected or at work, matching the source's present participle.

choices.english: to walk in holiness of heart
choices.why: Keeps 'holiness' for ὁσιότης and the infinitive 'to walk' for πορεύεσθαι, preserving the metaphor of conduct as a path.
rejected: to proceed in purity of heart
to go in sanctity of heart

choices.term: ἐπίφανον τὸ πρόσωπόν σου ἐφ' ἡμᾶς
choices.english: make your face shine upon us
choices.why: Uses the standard biblical idiom for divine favor, matching the aorist imperative and the face imagery.
Keeps the participle 'becoming' with the adjective 'obedient' to preserve the process sense of coming into submission.
Renders the feminine diminutive of παῖς as 'female slaves' to distinguish from δούλων ('male slaves') and preserve the gendered pairing.

bible_refs.note: ἐπίφανον τὸ πρόσωπόν σου ἐφ' ἡμᾶς echoes the psalm's plea for God's face to shine, though the exact wording differs.
The plea for God's face to shine and for mercy echoes the psalm's opening, though not a direct quotation.

pass_b_english: You have made the enduring order of the world visible through the things that are at work in it. You, Lord, created the inhabited earth. You are faithful in every generation, just in your judgments, wonderful in strength and majesty, wise in creating and understanding in establishing what has come to be, good in what is seen and kind to those who trust in you, merciful and compassionate. Forgive our lawless deeds, our injustices, our transgressions, and our offenses.

Do not count every sin of your male and female slaves, but cleanse us with the cleansing of your truth, and make our steps straight so that we walk in holiness of heart and do what is good and pleasing before you and before our rulers.

Yes, Master, make your face shine upon us for good in peace, so that we may be sheltered by your mighty hand and delivered from every sin by your uplifted arm, and rescue us from those who hate us unjustly.

Give harmony and peace to us and to all who dwell on the earth, just as you gave to our fathers when they called upon you in holiness, in faith and truth, so that we may become obedient to your almighty and glorious name and to our rulers and governors on the earth.

polish.changed: Broke the long first paragraph into shorter sentences so each divine attribute stands clearly, kept the prayer's four movements distinct, and preserved every petition and qualification exactly.

last_rejected.quote: Do not count every sin of your male and female slaves
last_rejected.source_quote: μὴ λογίσῃ πᾶσαν ἁμαρτίαν δούλων σου καὶ παιδισκῶν
last_rejected.why: Source says 'Do not reckon every sin of your servants and handmaids'; 'every' modifies 'sin', not 'slaves'.
last_rejected.fix: Do not count any sin of your male and female slaves
last_rejected.ruling: English 'every sin of your male and female slaves' correctly has 'every' modifying 'sin' (πᾶσαν ἁμαρτίαν), not slaves; 'male and female' accurately renders δούλων καὶ παιδισκῶν.

problems.quote: when they called upon you in holiness, in faith and truth, becoming obedient to your almighty and glorious name, and to our rulers and governors on the earth.
problems.source_quote: ἐπικαλουμένων σε αὐτῶν ὁσίως ἐν πίστει καὶ ἀληθείᾳ, ὑπηκόους γινομένους τῷ παντοκράτορι καὶ ἐνδόξῳ ὀνόματί σου, τοῖς τε ἄρχουσιν καὶ ἡγουμένοις ἡμῶν ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς.
problems.why: The accusative participle does not modify the fathers in the genitive absolute; it asks that we become obedient to God's name and to earthly rulers.
problems.fix: just as you gave to our fathers when they called upon you holily in faith and truth, so that we become obedient to your almighty and glorious name and to our rulers and governors on the earth.
problems.ruling: Accusative ὑπηκόους γινομένους cannot agree with genitive absolute ἐπικαλουμένων αὐτῶν; it modifies ἡμῖν (us). The English makes the fathers, not us, obedient to the name and to the rulers.

edits.old: when they called upon you in holiness, in faith and truth, becoming obedient to your almighty and glorious name, and to our rulers and governors on the earth.
edits.new: when they called upon you in holiness, in faith and truth, so that we may become obedient to your almighty and glorious name and to our rulers and governors on the earth.

fixed: agency is real: accusative ὑπηκόους γινομένους cannot agree with genitive ἐπικαλουμένων... αὐτῶν / dative πατράσιν, so it is us becoming obedient; changed dangling participle to purpose clause.
